ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are four synchronously connected JK flip-flops, labeled FF0, FF1, FF2, FF3, sharing the same CP clock line. The J and K inputs of each stage flip-flop are connected in a toggle-control form: the lowest bit FF0 has T0=1, so it toggles on every clock pulse; the toggle control of FF1 comes from Q0; before FF2 there is an AND gate G1, using the AND of the lower bits Q0 and Q1 as the toggle condition; before FF3 there is an AND gate G2, using the lower-bit AND signal as the toggle condition. The outputs on the right are respectively labeled Q0, Q1, Q2, Q3, and at the bottom there is also an AND gate G3, whose output is labeled C. Reasoning: These connections form a four-bit synchronous binary up counter. Initially all four flip-flops are 0, that is, Q3Q2Q1Q0=0000. Each time a CP pulse comes, the count value increases by 1. Therefore CP=15 means that after 15 pulses, the counting state is decimal 15, that is, Q3Q2Q1Q0=1111. At this time, the relevant Q outputs sent into the output AND gate G3 are all 1, so C=1.

method.method_draft: First describe the image as a four-stage synchronous JK counter: FF0 toggles every CP because T0=1; FF1 toggles when Q0=1; FF2 toggles when the AND of Q0 and Q1 is 1; FF3 toggles when the AND of the lower bits is 1. Recognize this as a 4-bit binary up-counter. From the text, the initial state is Q3Q2Q1Q0=0000 and the queried clock count is CP=15. After 15 pulses the 4-bit count is decimal 15, i.e. Q3Q2Q1Q0=1111. Since G3 is the output AND that forms C from the relevant Q outputs, C=1.
